# SEV-1 INCIDENT - RELEASE BLOCKER
**Title:** Statements are filing some payments under the wrong kind of transaction, or dropping the payee name
**Owner:** Payments Operations
**Disposition:** Do not ship this release until it is resolved

## What customers reported

Over the past few days support has collected a run of tickets that all share one
shape: the money itself moved fine, but the app files the payment under a category
that does not match what the customer actually did, or shows the wrong name - or
no name at all - beside it. In every case the row that misbehaves carries one very
particular, uncommon form of raw statement text; everyday rows are labeled exactly
as before. The tickets below are anonymized, but the raw narration each customer
pasted is reproduced verbatim, because that raw text is what makes each case
reproducible.

> "I wrote a cheque against my account and the app just lists it as a general
> transfer now - nothing marks it as a cheque anymore. My earlier cheques were
> tagged correctly. The only thing sitting in that row's note is the cheque's own
> number, nothing else around it."

> "My salary came in and the amount is right, but where my employer's name should
> be the app now just prints the word `NACH`. The raw text on that row looks like
> `ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES` - it used to lift the employer's name off the end
> of that reference, and now it is picking up the wrong piece of it."

> "On some transfers that come in, the sender's name is blank now. Those rows all
> share the same reference layout - a short block of letters, then a long string
> of digits, then the name - for example `GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR`. The name
> sitting at the end just is not being pulled through anymore; the name column
> comes out empty."

The same batch of complaints also covers two quieter cases that are about the
category rather than the name. The token confirmation charge a bank posts when a
new auto-debit mandate is set up - a small nominal amount, with the note flagging
it as a mandate - is being filed as an ordinary transfer instead of being
recognized as a verification entry. And a refund that came back on a card is
landing as a plain refund for some customers when it should read as a card
reversal; a customer on a different type of account sees the same kind of refund
labeled correctly, so the wrong label appears to depend on the account category.

## Scope of impact

Everyday activity - normal purchases, routine transfers, regular deposits - is
categorized and named correctly, which is precisely why this slipped through QA and
why our monitoring dashboards looked healthy. The breakage is confined to a small
set of unusual transaction forms - among them a note or reference that is exactly
a certain number of digits wide - each one hinging on some exact shape of the raw
row rather than anything about the customer, and each form individually uncommon. But they occur right across the customer base, so they
generate a steady trickle of "why is this labeled wrong" tickets and, more
damaging, they poison the spending-category summaries and payee histories that
several downstream features rely on. That combination is why we are treating it
as ship-blocking rather than a backlog item.

## What we need from engineering

The labeling path is fully deterministic and runs offline - hand it the same
transaction and it reproduces the same wrong answer every time - so each of these
is reproducible on demand and can be pinned down exactly. Get the affected forms
labeling and naming correctly again, and do it without disturbing any transaction
that is already labeled right today. A fix that rescues these cases but nudges the
behavior of ordinary, currently-correct transactions is not acceptable: the pass
condition is simply that the specific problem payments described above come out
right and everything else stays exactly where it is.

I have everything needed. Here is the full report.

---

# Overall flow

**Entry point: `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py`**
- A Flask app exposing `POST /categorizeTransaction` (line 69) and `POST /recurrentTransactions` (line 55).
- `categorizeTransaction` reads `bank`, `acc_type` (→ `accountType`), `accountUID`, `accountHolder`, `isPFMEnabled`, normalizes `transactions` into a pandas DataFrame, and cleans it via `AppUtil.clean_input_df` (line 87).
- It then dispatches on `bank` (a giant if/elif chain: `"ANDHRA_BANK"`, `"SBI"`, `"ICICI"`, `"HDFC"`, `"IDFC"`, `"BANK_OF_INDIA"`, `"IDBI"`, ..., `"INDUSIND"` at line 451, `"AXIS"` at line 427, etc.). Each branch runs the identical pipeline:
  1. `categorize_<Bank>_transactions(transactions, accountType)` — bank-specific `BankScripts/*.py`. Each of these builds a list of `[boolean-mask, choice]` pairs and applies `np.select(conditions, choices, default="TRANSFER")` to set `transactionCategory` (so anything unmatched **falls through to `TRANSFER`** — this is the "generic transfer" you're seeing), then similar `np.select` blocks for `transactionSubcategory` and `partyName`.
  2. If `accountType == "CREDIT_CARD"`: `card_clean_names()` (CardCleanNames.py) then `card_purpose()` (CardPurpose.py).
  3. `purpose(transactions, accountType)` (Purpose.py) — assigns/overrides `transactionSubcategory` (SALARY, LOAN, LOAN_REPAYMENT, INSURANCE, TECHNICAL_BOUNCE, ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION at Purpose.py:165, etc.) using regex constants from `RegexConstants.py`/`BankRegexConstants.py`.
  4. `clean_names(transactions, accountType, bank)` (CleanName.py, ~1971 lines) — normalizes `partyName` to canonical merchant/party names (e.g., "TataSky DTH", "HDFC Bank Loan ...").
  5. Optional: `internal_payment()` (fuzzy match of partyName vs accountHolder), `salary_detection()` for SAVING, and if PFM enabled `pfm_categorization()` + `simple_description()`.

**Helpers: `UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py`**
- `sep_by_dash(description, n1, n2)` (line 17-18): `description.str.split('-').str[n1:n2].str.join('')` — i.e., dash-token slice `[n1:n2]`.
- `py_extract(description, pat, index)` (lines 61-66): `description.str.extract(pat).get(index)`; **if the requested group index doesn't exist, `res is None` and it returns `pd.Series("")` — i.e., silently blank** (important for regression 3).

**Enums**
- `TransactionCategoryEnums.py`: display labels for categories, e.g. `CHEQUE_PAID="Cheque"` (line 27), `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT="Cheque"` (line 57), `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION="Account Verification"` (line 83), `REFUND="Refund"` (line 24), `CHEQUE_RETURN="Cheque Bounce"` (line 44), `AUTO_MANDATE_CHARGES="Auto Mandate Charges"` (line 84).
- `TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py`: subcategory labels, e.g. `SALARY`, `LOAN_REPAYMENT`, `INWARD_CHEQUE_RETURN` (line 37), `INTERNAL_PAYMENT` (line 57).

---

# Regression findings

## 1. Cheque detection: bare-digit narration falls through to TRANSFER

Bare-digit cheque numbers are matched against the `remark` column across banks. Prime suspect (the only rule using an **exact** fixed width, and the only bank missing its CREDIT twin):

**`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/Indusind.py` line 64:**
```python
64:  [transactions.remark.str.contains("^[0-9]{5}$",na=False, case=False) & transactions.type.eq("DEBIT") , "CHEQUE_PAID"],
```
- `^[0-9]{5}$` requires **exactly 5 digits**. A standard 6-digit Indian cheque number (e.g. `123456`) no longer matches, so the transaction hits the default at line 80: `np.select(..., default="TRANSFER")`.
- Every comparable bank uses a wider bracket **and** has a CREDIT→CHEQUE_DEPOSIT twin, which Indusind conspicuously lacks:
  - Axis.py:58-59 — `"^[0-9]{5,6}$"` DEBIT→CHEQUE_PAID / CREDIT→CHEQUE_DEPOSIT
  - PNB.py:60-61 — `"^[0-9]{5,6}$"` (both directions)
  - BankOfMaharashtra.py:73-74 — `"^[0-9]{5,6}$"` (both)
  - YES.py:52-53 and UCO.py:44-45 — `"^[0-9]{3,6}$"` (both)
- Likely original: `^[0-9]{5,6}$` (or `{6}`), plus the missing CREDIT line.

Other bare-digit cheque regexes worth knowing about (for completeness / secondary suspects):
- Kotak.py:65,67 — `"^[0-9]{3,5}$"` (excludes 6-digit; but consistent with Kotak.py:241 and 287, so likely original).
- RBL.py:49-50 — `"^[0-9]{1,3}$"` (odd but consistent with RBL.py:117).
- KarurVyasa.py:50-51 — `"^00[0-9]{4}$"` (6 digits but forces leading `00`).
- BOB.py:70 (`{3,5}` → CHEQUE_PAID) vs BOB.py:138 (`{3,4}$` for partyName) — internally inconsistent, but affects name, not category.
- IDBI.py:55-58 — cheque via description patterns (`"[0-9]{6}-|^WTHDRL,CLG|CHQ Paid"`), no bare-digit remark rule.

## 2. NACH salary name extraction: `ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES` → `NACH` (confirmed bug)

**`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/IDBI.py` line 83:**
```python
83:  [transactions.description.str.contains("^ACH-BD-NACH", na=False, case=False) , sep_by_dash(transactions.description,2,3)],
84:  [transactions.description.str.contains("^ACH-BD-", na=False, case=False) , sep_by_dash(transactions.description,2,3)],
```
- `sep_by_dash(d, 2, 3)` = dash tokens `[2:3]` (AppUtil.py:17-18). For `ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES` the tokens are `["ACH", "BD", "NACH", "ACME INDUSTRIES"]`, so `[2:3]` yields exactly **`NACH`** — the precise wrong output you described.
- Line 83 should be `sep_by_dash(transactions.description, 3, 4)` to grab token 3 (`ACME INDUSTRIES`). Line 84 (`^ACH-BD-<NAME>`, 3 tokens) correctly uses `(2,3)`; line 83 exists precisely to skip the extra `NACH` token, so `(2,3)` there is pointless as written.
- Cross-reference proving the intended semantics: HDFC handles the identical shape correctly — **HDFC.py:169**: `"^ACH D- BD-NACH-"` → `sep_by_dash(transactions.description,3,4)`.

## 3. Incoming transfer `GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR` → blank name (confirmed bug)

**`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/IDBI.py` line 110:**
```python
110: [transactions.description.str.contains("^[A-Z]{5}[0-9]{10,}", na=False, case=False) , py_extract(transactions.description, pat="[0-9]{10,} (.*)", index=1)],
```
- The condition `^[A-Z]{5}[0-9]{10,}` matches "short letter block (5 letters) + long digit string" (`GBHDL0123456789 ...`), so the rule fires.
- But the extraction pattern `"[0-9]{10,} (.*)"` has **only one capture group** (index 0), while `index=1` is requested. In `py_extract` (AppUtil.py:61-66), `str.extract(...).get(1)` returns `None`, hence `return pd.Series("")` — the name silently comes out **blank**.
- Fix direction: `index=0`. Confirmed as an outlier: every other `index=1` call in the codebase pairs with a two-group pattern (SBI.py:139,146,147; Kotak.py:150,175,233 e.g. `"(^CLG TO|^TO CLG) (.*)"`; ICICI.py:159,168 e.g. `"TRFR (TO|FROM):(.*)"`; BankOfMaharashtra.py:126; DCB.py:80-81). IDBI:110 is the only single-group pattern using `index=1`.
- (Related commented-out R heritage code showing the pattern family: StandardCharted.py:189-190 `"[0-9]{10,18} ([A-z].*)"`.)

## 4. Mandate token confirmation charge → ordinary transfer

Two "template twin" rules exist; they disagree on the token amount:

**`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/Axis.py` line 25 (prime suspect):**
```python
24:  [transactions.description.str.contains(BANK_VER, na=False, case=False) &  transactions.amount.isin([1,-1]) , "ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION"],
25:  [transactions.amount.eq(1) & transactions.description.str.contains("MANDATE|Mandate", na=False, case=False)  , "ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION"],
26:  [transactions.amount.isin([1]) & transactions.type.eq("CREDIT") , "ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION"],
```
**Compare the sibling template in `Indusind.py` lines 29-31:**
```python
29:  [transactions.description.str.contains(BANK_VER,na=False, case=False) &  transactions.amount.isin([1,-1]) , "ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION"],
30:  [transactions.amount.eq(2) & transactions.description.str.contains("MANDATE|Mandate",na=False, case=False)  , "ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION"],
31:  [transactions.amount.eq(1) & transactions.type.eq("DEBIT") , "ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION"],
```
- Axis and Indusind share an almost line-for-line template (same `MNDTVRFCHGS`→AUTO_MANDATE_CHARGES at Axis.py:28 / Indusind.py:33, same "Dr Card Charge", etc.). Indusind's mandate line uses `amount.eq(2)` (the classic Rs 2 mandate-token confirmation debit); Axis's uses `amount.eq(1)`, which is already redundant with the surrounding Rs 1 rules (lines 24 and 26 cover amount 1).
- Consequence on Axis: a Rs 2 debit with a "MANDATE" note matches nothing in the block — `BANK_VER` needs amount ∈ {1,-1}; line 25 needs amount == 1 — so it drops to `default="TRANSFER"` (Axis.py:76). Likely original: `transactions.amount.eq(2)` (or `isin([1,2])`).
- Related but distinct rules (not the bug): AUTO_MANDATE_CHARGES keyword rules at SBI.py:33, PNB.py:14, Kotak.py:39, BOI.py:21, ICICI.py:32, IDBI.py:33, Federal.py:21, etc.; `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION` assignment in Purpose.py:165.

## 5. Card refund not labeled as card reversal for savings accounts (confirmed bug)

**`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/Indusind.py` lines 26-27:**
```python
26:  [transactions.description.str.contains("\\bPOS TXN",na=False, case=False) & transactions.type.eq("CREDIT") & transactions.amount.ge(10) & (accountType=="SAVINGS") , "CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL"],
27:  [transactions.description.str.contains("\\bPOS TXN",na=False, case=False) & transactions.type.eq("CREDIT") & (accountType=="SAVING") , "REFUND"],
```
- Line 26 tests `accountType == "SAVINGS"` — but the account-type value used everywhere else in the codebase is **`"SAVING"`** (singular): Controller.py:106/130/... (`if accountType == "SAVING":`), Indusind.py:27 itself, Indusind.py:95 (`accountType=="CURRENT"`), HDFC.py:124, ICICI.py:105, SBI.py:156, Kotak.py:283, etc. No caller ever passes `"SAVINGS"`.
- So line 26 can never fire; every `POS TXN` credit (including ≥ Rs 10 card reversals) on a savings account falls to line 27 and is labeled plain **REFUND** instead of **CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL**. Fix direction: `"SAVINGS"` → `"SAVING"` on line 26.
- Related context: subcategory `CARD_RECEIPTS` for CURRENT accounts at Indusind.py:95; other card-reversal rules (not account-type dependent): HDFC.py:21 (`^POS.*RVSL|^CRV POS|^POS REF|UNCLAIM POSTXN` → CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL) vs HDFC.py:20 (same-ish match with `amount.lt(25)` → REFUND); IDBI.py:19 (`Rev.*pos/|RPAY-POS` → CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL).

---

# Summary table

| # | Bug | File:Line | Broken code | Expected |
|---|-----|-----------|-------------|----------|
| 1 | Bare-digit cheque narration → TRANSFER | `BankScripts/Indusind.py:64` | `remark.str.contains("^[0-9]{5}$") & DEBIT → CHEQUE_PAID` | width `{5,6}` (cf. Axis.py:58-59, PNB.py:60-61, BOM.py:73-74) + missing CREDIT→CHEQUE_DEPOSIT twin |
| 2 | `ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES` extracts `NACH` | `BankScripts/IDBI.py:83` | `sep_by_dash(description,2,3)` | `sep_by_dash(description,3,4)` (cf. HDFC.py:169) |
| 3 | `GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR` → blank name | `BankScripts/IDBI.py:110` | `py_extract(pat="[0-9]{10,} (.*)", index=1)` — pattern has only group 0; `py_extract` returns `""` for missing group (AppUtil.py:61-66) | `index=0` |
| 4 | Rs 2 mandate token charge → TRANSFER | `BankScripts/Axis.py:25` | `amount.eq(1) & "MANDATE|Mandate" → ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION` | `amount.eq(2)` (cf. twin template Indusind.py:30) |
| 5 | Savings card refund not labeled card reversal | `BankScripts/Indusind.py:26` | `(accountType=="SAVINGS") → CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL` — dead branch | `(accountType=="SAVING")` (value used by Controller.py and every other script) |

Note: since all bank scripts use `np.select(..., default="TRANSFER")` for `transactionCategory`, any narrowed/never-true condition manifests exactly as "falls through to generic transfer," which matches regressions 1 and 4; bugs 2/3 are `partyName`-extraction defects inside IDBI's `np.select` name block; bug 5 is a dead string comparison. No files were modified.

def mk(rows):
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    for col in ["description", "remark", "type"]:
        if col not in df:
            df[col] = ""
    df["amount"] = pd.to_numeric(df.get("amount", 0))
    df["balanceAfterTransaction"] = 0.0
    return df

    ok = actual == expected

    {"description": "TRANSFER WITHDRAWAL", "remark": "12345", "type": "DEBIT", "amount": 5000},    # 5-digit still works
    {"description": "TRANSFER WITHDRAWAL", "remark": "1234567", "type": "DEBIT", "amount": 5000},  # 7 digits: not a cheque, stays TRANSFER
])

check("Axis Rs1 credit (unchanged)", r.transactionCategory[2], "ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION")

Resolved. Each ticket traced to a single-line defect in the rule tables; five one-line fixes total, verified with a reproduction script (14/14 checks pass, including guards that ordinary transactions are untouched).

## Root causes and fixes

**1. Cheque filed as generic transfer** — `BankScripts/Indusind.py:64`
The bare-cheque-number rule matched a remark of **exactly 5 digits** (`^[0-9]{5}$`), so standard 6-digit cheque numbers fell through `np.select`'s `default="TRANSFER"`. Every sibling bank (Axis, PNB, Bank of Maharashtra) uses `{5,6}`. Fixed to `^[0-9]{5,6}$`. 5-digit remarks still match; 7+-digit remarks still stay TRANSFER.

**2. Salary payee shows `NACH`** — `BankScripts/IDBI.py:83`
For `ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES`, the rule took dash-token slice `[2:3]` — which is literally `NACH`. The rule exists precisely to skip that extra token (the generic `^ACH-BD-` rule on the next line correctly uses `[2:3]` for the 3-token form). Fixed to `sep_by_dash(..., 3, 4)` → `Acme Industries`. Matches HDFC's handling of the identical shape (HDFC.py:169).

**3. Blank sender name on `GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR`** — `BankScripts/IDBI.py:110`
The extraction pattern `"[0-9]{10,} (.*)"` has only one capture group (index 0), but the code requested `index=1`. `py_extract` (AppUtil.py:61-66) silently returns `""` for a missing group — hence the empty name column. Fixed to `index=0`. Every other `index=1` call in the codebase pairs with a two-group pattern; this was the lone outlier.

**4. Mandate token charge filed as transfer** — `BankScripts/Axis.py:25`
The mandate-confirmation rule required `amount.eq(1)` — redundant with the Rs 1 rules on the adjacent lines — so the Rs 2 mandate token debit matched nothing and defaulted to TRANSFER. The line-for-line twin template in Indusind.py:30 uses `amount.eq(2)`. Restored `eq(2)`; the Rs 1 penny-drop rules on lines 24/26 are untouched.

**5. Card refund not labeled card reversal on savings accounts** — `BankScripts/Indusind.py:26`
The reversal branch tested `accountType == "SAVINGS"`, but the value passed everywhere (Controller.py and every other bank script) is `"SAVING"` — a dead branch, so all POS-TXN credits on savings accounts fell to the plain REFUND rule below it. Fixed the string; ≥ Rs 10 POS credits now get CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL, sub-Rs-10 ones remain REFUND, and CURRENT-account behavior is unchanged (which is why other account types "saw it labeled correctly").
